title: Khanate of Sibir
capsule: The Khanate of Sibir was a Tatar successor state of the Golden Horde centred on the confluence of the Irtysh and Tobol rivers in western Siberia, established in the late fourteenth or early fifteenth century; by the mid-sixteenth century it was the dominant power among the indigenous Khanty and Mansi peoples of the Ob-Irtysh basin. Khan Kuchum, who seized power around 1563 and converted his subjects to Islam, initially paid tribute to the Tsardom of Russia but repudiated it in 1571 and killed a Russian envoy. Ermak Timofeevich's Cossack expedition of 1581–1582, financed by the Stroganov merchant family, routed Kuchum's forces at the Battle of Chuvash Cape and captured the khanate's capital Isker (Sibir); Kuchum continued guerrilla resistance until his final defeat in 1598, after which Russian colonization of Siberia proceeded rapidly.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The khanate's territorial extent is estimated from Russian conquest chronicles and early colonial administrative records; as a lightly administered steppe-taiga polity with tribute-collecting rather than garrison-based rule, precise pre-conquest boundaries are conjectural.
